funder: NLnet Foundation (European Commission DG CNECT funding)
amountText: between 5.000 and 50.000 EUR per project; about 400,000 EUR reserved for open calls
eligibility: Independent researchers, developers and organisations proposing free and open source work auxiliary to CodeSupply's goal of current, correct, openly published software package metadata (origin, licensing, vulnerabilities, quality). As an EU-funded NLnet fund it requires a European dimension, usually meaning an applicant from a Horizon Europe eligible country; applicants elsewhere must explain how the project meets it.
geography: Worldwide in principle, European dimension required (normally Horizon Europe eligible countries)
entityTypes: Individuals, collectives, associations, foundations, NGOs, universities, public sector, cooperatives, SMEs, corporations
process: 1. Check the project fits CodeSupply and NLnet general requirements. 2. Fill in the NLnet online form at nlnet.nl/propose, selecting the CodeSupply fund, in plain English text in your own words. 3. Submit before 2026-11-03 12:00 CET. 4. NLnet reviews in rounds and may send follow-up questions. 5. Selected projects agree a milestone plan; grants are paid against completed milestones.
requiredMaterials: Proposal title
Project website(s) / repositories
Project summary and expected results (max 1,000 characters)
Requested amount in EUR (5,000-50,000 for a first grant)
Budget breakdown: tasks, effort, hourly/daily/monthly rate, expenses (max 4,000 characters)
Comparison with existing efforts and what is new (max 4,000 characters)
Expected technical challenges (max 4,000 characters)
Ecosystem, dependencies, engagement and main users (max 2,000 characters)
Relevant experience (max 2,000 characters)
Other funding sources (max 1,000 characters)
Optional attachments (HTML, PDF, ODF, images, plain text; 50 MB total)
Generative AI disclosure; if used, prompts and AI output (max 8,000 characters or files up to 50 MB)
Contact: name or pseudonym, email, phone with country code, optional OpenPGP key
Applicant type, organisation name and country
decisionTime: unconfirmed: NLnet does not state it on the fund page; past NLnet calls typically announced first-round selection within about 2-3 months of the deadline
obligations: All project results must be released under a recognised free or open source licence and fit CodeSupply's goals and the Open Internet Stack; work is delivered and paid per agreed milestone; no equity.
forkmeshAngle: Propose a FOSS component that publishes signed, integrity-checked provenance metadata for mirrored Git repositories (source origin, mirror attestations, licence detection) as open data that CodeSupply's federated catalog can ingest. CodeSupply exists to curate package origin and supply-chain metadata, and ForkMesh's signed mirrors already produce exactly this kind of origin evidence.
risks: CodeSupply is a separate fund from NLnet Restack (also on this list): both are open in the same NLnet call (deadline 2026-11-03) and use the same nlnet.nl/propose form, where the applicant selects the fund; this entry is only the CodeSupply option, and the same work must not be submitted to both. Small pot (about 400,000 EUR total) and a narrow scope: the proposal must be auxiliary to package-metadata curation, not general ForkMesh development. European dimension needed if the entity is outside Horizon Europe countries. NLnet says work (mostly) generated by LLMs is ineligible under its current GenAI policy, which is being revised; ForkMesh's AI-agent workflow must be disclosed and could be an obstacle. Results must be FOSS (MIT is fine).

funder: Sovereign Tech Agency (German Federal Ministry funded)
amountText: The cost of the work described in the application must exceed EUR 50,000 (current minimum); no maximum stated
eligibility: Maintainers, organisations or communities behind open digital base technologies that other software depends on (libraries, package managers, protocol implementations, developer/admin tools, encryption). Code must be under an OSI-approved or FSF free licence; activities already funded by another public entity are excluded; prototypes and user-facing applications (e.g. messaging apps, file storage services) are not currently sought.
geography: Worldwide (the Agency says it invests globally and works with people, companies and FOSS communities everywhere)
entityTypes: unconfirmed: page names no restriction; FAQ refers to people, companies and FOSS communities
process: 1. Create an account on apply.sovereign.tech and submit the application (German or English) through the portal only. 2. Basic requirements check, then review against criteria (prevalence, relevance, vulnerability, public interest, activities, expertise), up to 10 weeks. 3. Scoping phase with a program manager to define the project description. 4. External expert consultation for final selection, up to 8 weeks. 5. Legal compliance review, supporting documents and contracting, up to 8 weeks; work starts only after the contract is signed.
requiredMaterials: Online portal application in English or German (form preview: Application-Form-Sovereign-Tech-Fund-1-November-2024.pdf)
Description of the technology and its role as a dependency for other software (prevalence, relevance)
Vulnerability / risk the investment addresses and public interest argument
Planned activities with cost exceeding EUR 50,000
Team expertise and maintainer information
Licence information (OSI or FSF approved; docs not CC NC/ND)
Declaration of other public funding for the same activities
Supporting legal/compliance documentation during contracting
decisionTime: About 6 months from submission to potential contract start (up to 10 weeks review, up to 8 weeks expert consultation, up to 8 weeks legal and contracting)
obligations: Contract with scope and milestones agreed in scoping; regular progress reports tied to invoicing and a final report; payment within up to 30 days of approved invoice and report; work must stay under an OSI/FSF licence; no equity.
forkmeshAngle: Pitch the ForkMesh mirror protocol and its library layer (signed, integrity-checked Git mirroring and the signed issue/PR record format) as base infrastructure that keeps any Git-hosted dependency reachable when its source host fails, not the desktop app. The fund's criteria reward reducing vulnerability of technologies many projects depend on, which matches source-availability resilience for the open source supply chain.
risks: Funds established, widely depended-on technology; prototypes and user-facing apps are explicitly not sought, and ForkMesh's adoption is early, so 'prevalence' will be weak. Large competition and a ~6 month process. Entity-type rules and contract type (likely a service contract under German public procurement rules) are not stated on the page. Commercial hosted tier must be kept separate from the funded open source work.

amountText: In-kind services, no cash amount stated: technical debt management, memory safety transition, post-quantum readiness, Cyber Resilience Act compliance, security audits, supply chain security, bug and fix bounties (bounties paused as of Sept 2026)
eligibility: Open source projects meeting the program criteria (critical, widely used open digital infrastructure) whose maintainers agree to the participation rules; projects can also be invited after another Sovereign Tech Agency program or recommended by a service provider.
geography: unconfirmed: no geographic restriction stated on the page
entityTypes: unconfirmed: project maintainers / communities; entity type not stated
process: 1. Read the criteria and participation rules. 2. Create an account on the application portal and submit the application (preview PDF available). 3. Ongoing review; ineligible projects are declined, eligible ones invited to join. 4. Work is scoped individually with the project and an implementation partner. 5. Start depends on partner capacity and demand.
requiredMaterials: Portal application form (preview PDF on the program page)
Project description and evidence against the program criteria
Requested services (e.g. security audit, supply chain security, CRA compliance, technical debt)
Confirmation of the participation rules
Maintainer agreement to the work
decisionTime: unconfirmed: applications reviewed on an ongoing basis; start depends on partner capacity
obligations: Follow the participation rules; all work is done in agreement with the project's maintainers; no cash, no equity.
forkmeshAngle: Request a security audit and supply-chain security review of the ForkMesh mirror signing and integrity-check code paths. A third-party audit would strengthen the product's core trust claim, and the program exists to harden open source infrastructure.
risks: Services only, no money. Criteria favour critical, widely used dependencies; an early-stage project is unlikely to be accepted. Bug bounty platform paused for new reports (status Sept 2026, backlog ending fall 2026). Start times depend on partner capacity.

amountText: Freelance: hourly rate negotiated at market rates, 3-12 months, 6-32 h/week. Employment: TVoeD-Bund based, EUR 64,000 to 82,000 per year full-time, 2-year contracts, 20-40 h/week (up to three positions)
deadline: Next call expected 2027 (unconfirmed; 2026 round closed 2026-04-06, next round to be announced via newsletter and social media)

geography: Freelance: unconfirmed, apparently worldwide; Employment: Germany only
entityTypes: Individuals only (organisations are pointed to the Sovereign Tech Fund)
process: 1. Apply via the online portal in English during the open window (one application per person; no email materials). 2. Shortlist and video interviews. 3. Decisions and offers (2026 round: interviews from late April, offers by mid-May). 4. Contract start (freelance contract or employment with Sovereign Tech Agency GmbH).
requiredMaterials: Online portal application in English
Evidence of verifiable open source maintainer / community / technical writing work
Projects worked on and their licences
Proposed fellowship work (sustainability, mentoring, onboarding, technical improvements)
Track choice (freelance or employment) and availability in hours/week
decisionTime: About 5-6 weeks after the deadline (2026: deadline Apr 6, offers by May 15)
obligations: Work on project sustainability; take part in events, communications, interviews and evaluation reporting; join the maintainers community; full-time fellows also advise on Agency program design.
forkmeshAngle: A ForkMesh maintainer could apply as a freelance fellow to work on the open mirror protocol, contributor onboarding and documentation. The fellowship pays maintainers of open infrastructure, but it funds the person, not the company.
risks: Closed until a 2027 round is announced (dates unconfirmed). Individual-only and cannot be used by a company to fund its employees; requires an established maintainer track record on widely used infrastructure. Employment track Germany-only.

program: Prototype Fund (Germany), Jahrgang 03: Innovation, Up and Coming, and Resilience lines

entityTypes: Individuals and small teams (max 4 people); unconfirmed: companies and organisations cannot be the grantee
process: 1. Optional info sessions (19 Oct 2026 general, 22 Oct 2026 FLINTA*). 2. Choice of funding line (Innovation, Up and Coming, Resilience)

forkmeshAngle: Apply in the Resilience line with ForkMesh's decentralised Git collaboration (signed in-repo issues and PRs plus live signed mirrors) as an open source alternative to centralised Big Tech code hosting. The line was created for exactly this kind of de-centralising alternative.

Funds individuals, likely only those living or taxed in Germany; a ForkMesh company cannot be the grantee, so team members would need to qualify personally. Prototype stage focus; long gap to funding start (June 2027).

program: Fast Forward (free services for open source projects)
amountText: Free and discounted Fastly services (CDN, edge compute, security); no dollar value stated
eligibility: Open source projects, and the nonprofits/foundations that support them, judged on being open (licence and collaboration values), community-centred, and built on trust (secure, trustworthy processes). Commercial companies are not mentioned as eligible.
entityTypes: Open source projects and supporting nonprofits; for-profit eligibility unconfirmed
process: 1. Fill in the eligibility form on the Fast Forward page. 2. Fastly reviews eligibility against the open / community-centred / built-on-trust criteria. 3. Fastly contacts the project about its technical needs. 4. Services are provisioned free or discounted.
requiredMaterials: Fast Forward eligibility form (fields not shown on the public page; unconfirmed: project name, repository, licence, contact, description of needs)
Description of technical needs (traffic, CDN / edge compute requirements) on follow-up
decisionTime: unconfirmed: not stated
obligations: unconfirmed: none stated on the page (past participants typically acknowledge Fastly); services only, no cash, no equity.
forkmeshAngle: Ask for CDN and edge capacity to serve public clones, release artifacts and the signed mirror index of the open ForkMesh network, so the free public clone tier scales without the fleet's own bandwidth bill. Fastly's program exists to back open source projects with an open-internet mission, and ForkMesh's mirror network is open infrastructure.
risks: In-kind services only, value unstated. Eligibility targets open source projects and nonprofits; ForkMesh's paid hosted tier may make a for-profit applicant ineligible, so apply for the open protocol/public clone project. Git smart-HTTP traffic may not cache well on a CDN.

amountText: up to $1 million per year in total; a project can apply for up to $100,000 in one year, minimum $10,000 and multiples of $25,000 thereafter
deadline: Rolling (reviewed at the end of each quarter; next review end of Dec 2026)
eligibility: Individuals, projects, groups, communities or organisations maintaining existing, widely used and impactful Free/Libre and Open Source projects; very new projects or those with minimal usage are not considered for now. The recipient needs a bank account and the tax documents its jurisdiction requires.
geography: Worldwide (unconfirmed: no restriction stated; Indian tax paperwork applies for disbursement)
entityTypes: Individuals, groups, communities, organisations; for-profit eligibility unconfirmed
process: 1. Write a funding.json manifest following the fundingjson.org schema. 2. Publish it on the project website or repository (with the domain/well-known verification the schema provides). 3. Submit its URL at dir.floss.fund/submit. 4. The internal investment committee reviews submissions at the end of each quarter and emails the decision. 5. If accepted, tax and residency paperwork, up to 4 weeks, then disbursement.
requiredMaterials: funding.json manifest (fundingjson.org schema): entity block (type, role, name, email, description, webpage URL)
projects block: name, description, webpage and repository URLs, licences, tags
funding block: payment channels, funding plans (amount, currency, frequency), funding history
Domain / repository ownership verification for the listed URLs
Bank account and jurisdiction tax documents (after acceptance)
decisionTime: Quarterly: decision at the end of the quarter of submission, then up to 4 weeks of paperwork
obligations: Tax and residency paperwork before payment; public acknowledgement with a link/badge requested but not required; no reporting conditions stated; no equity.
forkmeshAngle: List ForkMesh's open mirror protocol and node software in funding.json and request USD 35,000-60,000 for maintenance of the signed mirroring and in-repo collaboration record format. Low effort since the manifest is reusable for other funders, and FLOSS/fund backs FOSS that the wider ecosystem relies on.
risks: Explicitly favours existing, widely used projects and skips very new or minimally used ones, which hurts an early-stage project. Most recent update on the official site is October 2025, so 2026 tranche activity is unconfirmed. Company-backed / commercial projects not addressed. Low effort makes it worth submitting anyway.

obligations: Participation in a 12-month cohort with mentorship; unconfirmed: reporting and open licensing requirements per call.

Mozilla funds open-web alternatives to concentrated platforms, which matches ForkMesh's mission.

Mozilla Ventures (equity investment) is the other running channel but is not a grant.

Accurate contact information for due diligence
Proof of a proper open source licence and public source code

Progress reports during the grant

OpenSats funds censorship-resistant FOSS that the Bitcoin and Nostr ecosystems depend on.

eligibility: Organisations worldwide aligned with Ford's programs, selected by the foundation; Ford does not accept unsolicited grant proposals by mail, email or phone. Technology and Society historically funds civil society and technically skilled nonprofits working on digital rights, equity, privacy, free expression and public-interest technology.
entityTypes: unconfirmed: in practice nonprofits / civil society organisations; for-profit eligibility not stated

Become visible to the Technology and Society team through public-interest technology networks, convenings and grantee partners. 3. If invited, the foundation runs its own program-specific selection and due diligence.

decisionTime: unconfirmed: not published
obligations: unconfirmed: standard Ford grant agreement with narrative and financial reporting; no equity.
forkmeshAngle: Long shot only: position ForkMesh's censorship-resistant, provider-independent Git hosting as public-interest infrastructure for civil society and digital rights groups whose code could be taken offline. Ford cares about digital rights and free expression, but it would fund a nonprofit steward, not a startup.

eligibility: Open source / open science / public-interest technology projects whose mission aligns with CS&S; the project joins CS&S, a US 501(c)(3) public charity, which holds funds on its behalf. Directory listing mentions an advisory group and a minimum budget (unconfirmed: exact threshold).
geography: unconfirmed: US-based sponsor; non-US projects not explicitly excluded on the official page
entityTypes: Unincorporated open source projects (charitable activity); not a for-profit company itself (the project would be a charitable program under CS&S)
process: 1. Read the Fiscally Sponsored Projects FAQ and the 'Timeline and Application Requirements' document. 2. Submit the New Project Inquiry Form. 3. Discovery conversation(s) with CS&S staff on mission fit, budget and governance. 4. Formal application and review. 5. Sign fiscal sponsorship agreement; funds and grants then flow through CS&S.
requiredMaterials: New Project Inquiry Form (project description, mission, team)
Items listed in the CS&S 'Timeline and Application Requirements' document (unconfirmed: exact list)
Project budget / expected funding sources (directory notes a minimum budget)
Advisory group / governance description (per directory listing)
decisionTime: unconfirmed: multi-step onboarding, typically weeks to a few months
obligations: Administrative fee on incoming funds (15%/20% per directory, unconfirmed); funds must be spent on charitable purposes under CS&S oversight; grant reporting and tax compliance handled with CS&S; project governance expectations.
forkmeshAngle: Place the open protocol and public-clone/mirror network (the free, MIT-licensed commons part of ForkMesh) under CS&S as a charitable open infrastructure project, so ForkMesh can take foundation money (e.g. Sloan, Ford, Sovereign Tech-type funds) that requires a 501(c)(3). CS&S specialises in open research and digital infrastructure and its Incubator focuses on governance and community health for such projects.
risks: Fiscal sponsorship requires separating a charitable open-source project from the commercial ForkMesh hosted service and crypto payout pool; a for-profit startup cannot itself be sponsored. Fees 15-20%. The Digital Infrastructure Incubator (Event Fund also not listed) has no announced 2026 cohort; CS&S says it is seeking funders for future cohorts.

funder: Open Source Collective (fiscal host on the Open Collective platform)
program: Fiscal hosting for open source projects (Open Collective funding channel; also receives GitHub Sponsors, thanks.dev, Open Source Pledge and company payouts)
amountText: No grant itself; a funding channel. Fixed 10% host fee on incoming funds, no setup fees or minimum balances; payment processor fees extra.
eligibility: Original or substantially forked open source project with recent activity or significant usage, OSI/FSF/Debian/Fedora-recognised license, hosted in an organisation repository (not a personal account), applicant must be a maintainer; two or more admins preferred. Not for business transactions benefiting an individual or customer.
geography: Worldwide (except sanctioned countries); funds held in USD; can pay non-US maintainers
entityTypes: Unincorporated open source projects / communities (the project, not a company, is hosted; for-profit status not addressed by OSC docs)
process: 1. Read the Terms of Fiscal Sponsorship and fee page; confirm eligibility. 2. Line up at least two community members as admins. 3. Create the collective and apply at opencollective.com/opensource/apply/intro. 4. Verify via GitHub OAuth (clear cases auto-approved) or request manual verification with project description and links. 5. OSC reviews (aims for weekly review; a few business days). 6. Collective goes live; set up tiers, link GitHub Sponsors / thanks.dev / company funders.
requiredMaterials: Agreement to Terms of Fiscal Sponsorship
GitHub authentication of an organisation repository (or manual verification request)
Manual path: description of the project and its goals, links to repositories, website and social accounts
Collective profile: name, slug, description, admins (2+ preferred)
Encouraged: CONTRIBUTING guide, code of conduct, documented decision-making process
decisionTime: Automatic to a few business days (weekly review target)
obligations: 10% host fee; expenses must be submitted publicly with receipts/invoices on the transparent ledger; funds must serve the open source project, not private business benefit; crypto only case-by-case via Drips; payments to sanctioned countries not possible.
forkmeshAngle: Open a 'forkmesh' collective for the MIT-licensed protocol and public mirror network so individual sponsors, companies (Open Source Pledge members) and thanks.dev dependency-funders can pay into a transparent ledger that covers mirror-fleet hosting and contributor bounties. It is the lowest-effort way to make ForkMesh fundable by the wider open source funding ecosystem.
risks: The repo must sit under an organisation account and be open source; funds cannot pay for the commercial hosted service or benefit the startup as a business. Crypto/Solana payout pool would not be supported (crypto case-by-case only via Drips). Money raised is donor-driven, not guaranteed.

program: Open Source Pledge: companies pay USD 2,000+ per developer per year to open source maintainers of their choosing
amountText: Member companies pay at least USD 2,000 per year per full-time-equivalent developer to open source maintainers and foundations of their choosing; cash only. Pledge reports USD 7,421,535 raised in total, over USD 3M in the past year. Per-project amounts are at each member company's discretion.
deadline: Rolling (member companies choose recipients, typically annually)
eligibility: No application for maintainers; member companies choose which maintainers/projects to pay. A project needs a public way to receive money (e.g. GitHub Sponsors, Open Collective, thanks.dev; unconfirmed: exact channels accepted).
geography: Worldwide (depends on the paying company and payout channel)
entityTypes: Open source maintainers, projects and foundations (recipient chosen by companies)
process: 1. Set up public funding channels (GitHub Sponsors and/or an Open Source Collective page) and a FUNDING.yml. 2. Identify Pledge member companies listed on opensourcepledge.com that use Git hosting / supply-chain tooling. 3. Contact them with a short case for funding ForkMesh's open protocol and mirror network. 4. Companies pay directly and report the payment in their annual Pledge report.
requiredMaterials: Public funding channel (GitHub Sponsors, Open Collective, etc.)
FUNDING.yml in the repository
Short funding pitch for member companies (what the money pays for)
decisionTime: At each member company's discretion (annual cycles)
obligations: None formal for recipients; payments are intended to be no-strings-attached. Member companies publish an annual report of their payments.
forkmeshAngle: Pitch Pledge member companies (many are developer-tool and infrastructure companies) to fund ForkMesh's independent mirror network as a supply-chain resilience measure for the Git dependencies they rely on. Works best once ForkMesh has an Open Source Collective page and GitHub Sponsors as receiving channels.
risks: No application route: income depends on companies choosing ForkMesh, which favours widely used dependencies over a young project. Payments to a for-profit startup may not count as a payment to an open source maintainer under Pledge norms; receive via a fiscal host for the open-source part.

Project Summary whose last line is a prioritised list of 2-5 keywords starting 'Keywords:' separated by semicolons

SMEs must carry at least 50% of total project cost, and no participant or country may exceed 70% of the budget. Civil purposes only; max 36 months.
geography: Eurostars countries (at least one EU or Horizon Europe associated country in the consortium)
entityTypes: SME lead (for-profit); partners can be companies, universities, research organisations
process: 1. Build an international consortium with an innovative SME as lead. 2. Check each partner's National Funding Body rules (some need national forms). 3. Submit the Eurostars application by the 4 March 2027 cut-off (Call 12 opens 17 Dec 2026 per secondary source). 4. Independent expert evaluation. 5. National funding bodies decide and sign contracts with each partner.
requiredMaterials: Eurostars application form on the Eureka platform (sections and limits per Call 12 guidelines: unconfirmed)
Per-participant budget and effort split meeting the 50% SME and 70% maximum rules
National eligibility documents for each participant's funding body (unconfirmed)
Consortium agreement (unconfirmed timing)
decisionTime: unconfirmed
obligations: Set by each National Funding Body (reporting, cost claims); the project must be civilian and finish within 36 months.
forkmeshAngle: Team up with a European SME or research group (e.g., a forge, CI or supply-chain security company) to co-develop interoperable signed-mirror and federation features between ForkMesh and their product. Eurostars funds market-oriented cross-border SME R&D, which suits a protocol meant to link independent hosts.
risks: Needs a foreign partner and an SME lead. National budgets and rules vary and can run out. ForkMesh's entity country is unknown, so its own national funder is unknown. The 2027 cut-off date comes from the official page, but the opening date is from a secondary source.

funder: European Cybersecurity Competence Centre (ECCC), Digital Europe Programme (European Commission)
program: DIGITAL-ECCC-2027-DEPLOY-CYBER-11-EULEG: Strengthening EU cybersecurity capacities & capabilities in line with legislative requirements (Cyber Resilience Act, NIS 2, etc.)
amountText: Requested EU contribution expected EUR 3-5 million per project (topic budget EUR 20 million; call total up to EUR 96 million); Simple Grant at 50% funding rate
eligibility: Legal entities (public or private) established in EU Member States (including OCTs) or EEA countries (Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein). They must not be directly or indirectly controlled from a non-eligible country (security restrictions under Article 12(5)). Single applicants are allowed; multi-country consortia are not required but help the impact score. All work, including subcontracting, must take place in eligible countries.
geography: EU Member States and EEA only; no control from outside
entityTypes: Companies, non-profits, public bodies, universities (legal entities only; no individuals)
process: 1. Register every beneficiary in the Participant Register (PIC) and pass validation. 2. Optionally build a consortium (e.g., with a National Coordination Centre, CSIRT or conformity assessment body). 3. Write Part B (max 70 pages) with the topic-mandatory KPIs. 4. Submit on the EU Funding & Tenders Portal by 14 January 2027, 17:00 CET. 5. Evaluation February-March 2027; results April 2027. 6. Grant agreement signature around October 2027.
requiredMaterials: Application Form Part A (administrative data, budget)
Application Form Part B technical description, max 70 pages
Topic-mandatory KPIs on the KPI template (e.g., stakeholders supported in implementing EU cybersecurity law, broken down by SMEs and start-ups, authorities, conformity assessment bodies)
Milestones and deliverables per the call guidance
Declaration on ownership and control for every entity
Legal status and origin documents for PIC validation
Budget at the 50% funding rate (equipment by depreciation only)
decisionTime: Results about 3 months after the deadline (April 2027); grant agreement around October 2027
obligations: 50% co-financing; KPI reporting; security and possible IPR restrictions; all activities in eligible countries.
forkmeshAngle: Propose open, low-cost Cyber Resilience Act compliance tooling built on ForkMesh for EU SMEs and open-source stewards: signed release provenance with SBOMs, signed vulnerability-handling records kept in the repository, and mirrored source availability for coordinated vulnerability disclosure. The topic text explicitly asks for SBOM, CVD and CSAF automation and user-friendly CRA compliance tools.
risks: Needs an EU or EEA entity not controlled from outside. 50% co-funding of a EUR 3-5M project is very large for a small team. Competition from established security vendors and national bodies is strong. Fits best as a partner in a consortium led by a CRA-focused organisation.

amountText: Total eligible project costs GBP 150,000 - 250,000; grant up to 70% (micro/small), 60% (medium); competition pot up to GBP 3.1 million; Phase 2 (invite only) up to GBP 1 million
eligibility: UK-registered micro, small or medium enterprises applying alone; no subcontractors and one application per SME. Work must be done and exploited in the UK. The project must start at TRL 1-3, with AI/ML as the core technical contribution; routine integration of existing tools or third-party models is excluded. It must fit one theme and one priority, e.g., Theme 4 AI safety and assurance, 'agentic runtime control and action assurance'.
entityTypes: UK-registered SMEs (for-profit) only
process: 1. Confirm the fit to Theme 4 and one priority. 2. Fill in the Innovation Funding Service application (questions 1-17, scope, summary). 3. Upload appendices. 4. Submit by 11 November 2026, 11:00 UK time. 5. Assessor scoring; about a 2% success chance. 6. Decision on 26 January 2027; project setup and Grant Offer Letter; project runs 1-3 months starting by 1 April 2027.
requiredMaterials: Project summary (400 words) and public description (400 words)
Scope (800 words): market, IP and defensibility, technical novelty and benchmarked validation, new-to-world capability, one key uncertainty
Q1-Q7 unscored: themes, applicant location, animal testing, permits and licences, international collaboration, export licence, Trusted Research and Innovation
Q8 IP position, freedom to operate and defensibility (400 words)
Q9 Need, technical development, validation and outputs (800 words) plus appendix of max 2 A4 pages with architecture diagram and validation/benchmark matrix
Q10 Team and resources (600 words) plus one-page CV per known team member
Q11 Market awareness, Q12 Outcomes and route to market, Q13 Wider impacts (400 words each)
Q14 Project management (400 words) plus Gantt chart appendix of max 2 A4 pages
Q15 Risks (400 words) plus risk register appendix of max 2 A4 pages
Q16 Added value and Q17 Costs and value for money (400 words each)
Project costs within GBP 150,000-250,000 total eligible costs; no URLs allowed in answers
decisionTime: Decision on 26 January 2027 (about 11 weeks after close)
obligations: Technical whitepaper at the end (progress, validation, IP defensibility, Phase 2 readiness). Subsidy-control compliance (Streamlined Subsidy Scheme SC10780). Project setup checks; no work before the Grant Offer Letter. Project must end by 30 June 2027.
forkmeshAngle: Under Theme 4 'agentic runtime control and action assurance', propose new ML methods that constrain and verify the actions of autonomous coding agents running in isolated worktrees, e.g., learned gating of agent commits and PRs with signed audit trails. This only fits if ForkMesh builds genuinely new AI/ML rather than integrating Codex or Claude Code.
risks: Replaces Smart grants, paused since January 2025 with no any-sector successor grant. Of 30 open Innovation Funding Service competitions, none is about open-source or software infrastructure. About a 2% success rate. AI/ML must be the core novelty. UK SME only. Projects are very short (1-3 months). The UK-Germany Bilateral CR&D Round 5 (any sector, closes 1 Dec 2026) is an alternative if there is a German SME partner.

funder: UK Government Sovereign AI Unit (Department for Science, Innovation and Technology) with the National Cyber Security Centre
program: Sovereign AI R&D Procurement Scheme (challenge: agent security and resilience testing / enabling safe AI agent adoption)
amountText: Contracts GBP 250,000 - 10 million, most around GBP 1-3 million; scheme budget up to GBP 100 million to March 2030; upfront payments possible
deadline: First batch closed 2026-10-01; further challenge competitions expected in later phases (dates unconfirmed)
eligibility: British AI companies, including start-ups, with demonstrator-stage technology. There is no minimum turnover, net asset or cash reserve requirement. The formal UK establishment requirement is unconfirmed.
entityTypes: UK AI companies (for-profit), including start-ups
process: 1. Watch sovereignai.gov.uk and UK tender notices (Find a Tender / Contracts Finder) for the next challenge competitions. 2. Attend the supplier briefing. 3. Submit a proposal through the streamlined procurement process by the batch deadline (documents unconfirmed). 4. Win a pre-commercial R&D contract with the challenge-owning department (develop, test, pilot, validate).
requiredMaterials: unconfirmed: tender response in the format set by each competition notice
Evidence that the technology is at demonstrator stage and ready for real-world testing
Proposed approach for the challenge (e.g., evidence-based, ideally automated agent risk management for CISOs covering resilience and cyber risk)
decisionTime: unconfirmed
obligations: Pre-commercial R&D contract deliverables and validation with the department; the supplier keeps its IP and is encouraged to commercialise it.
forkmeshAngle: If the NCSC agent-security challenge reruns, propose ForkMesh's isolated-worktree agent runner with signed, reviewable PR trails as an open-source control architecture that lets CISOs constrain, monitor and audit coding agents. The challenge text prefers solutions built on open-source frameworks for wide adoption.
risks: This is procurement, not a grant. It targets British AI companies. The first batch has closed and future challenges may change. No dedicated UKRI sovereign or open-source software fund is open: the Research Software Maintenance Fund round 2 closed in February 2026 and targets software used in UK research, and the AIRR open access call (compute only) closed in July 2026.

program: NRC Industrial Research Assistance Program (IRAP), financial support for technology innovation
amountText: Not stated on the NRC page; secondary summaries cite CAD 50,000 - 1,000,000 for regular IRAP projects (unconfirmed)
eligibility: Incorporated, for-profit businesses operating in Canada with up to 500 full-time equivalent employees that develop and commercialise technology-driven products or services and will create economic benefits in Canada. ULCs, LLCs, sole proprietorships, partnerships and cooperatives are not eligible. Work outside Canada and day-to-day operating costs are not funded.
entityTypes: Canadian incorporated for-profit SMEs only
process: 1. A senior executive calls the NRC contact centre (1-877-994-4727) to check readiness. 2. Meet a client engagement advisor, who may refer you on. 3. Work with an industrial technology advisor (ITA), who assesses vision, team and innovation potential. 4. If invited, submit a project proposal; an invitation does not guarantee funding. 5. Funding agreement.
requiredMaterials: CRA business number
Business plan
Recent financial statements
Business ownership structure details
Résumés or profiles of the management and technical team
Project proposal when invited by the ITA (format unconfirmed)
decisionTime: unconfirmed
obligations: unconfirmed: the page does not describe post-award reporting or claims terms; work must happen in Canada.
forkmeshAngle: If ForkMesh is or becomes a Canadian corporation, an ITA could co-fund Canadian developer salaries for R&D on the mirror fleet, signed-record protocol and desktop node. IRAP backs technology R&D with commercial potential and benefits to Canada.
risks: Needs a Canadian corporation operating in Canada. Funding is advisor-led and discretionary, with no published amounts. Only Canadian work is eligible.

funder: German federal government EXIST programme, administered by Projekttraeger Juelich (PtJ)
amountText: 12-month personal stipend: EUR 3,000/month (doctoral), EUR 2,500 (graduates), EUR 2,000 (vocational qualification), EUR 1,000 (students), plus EUR 150 per child; material costs up to EUR 10,000 (individual) or EUR 30,000 (team); EUR 5,000 coaching
eligibility: Founders from German universities and research institutions: scientists, graduates or former academic staff up to five years after graduating or leaving, and students at least halfway through their studies. Teams of up to three people. Applications go through the university or research institution's start-up network. Secondary sources say the company must not yet be founded (unconfirmed in the official text fetched).
entityTypes: Individuals and founding teams via a German university or research institution; not existing companies
process: 1. Join a German university or research institution's start-up service (Gruendungsnetzwerk) and find an academic mentor. 2. Write the idea paper with the start-up office. 3. The institution submits the application to PtJ. 4. Review and decision. 5. 12-month stipend with a workspace at the institution.
requiredMaterials: Idea paper on the technology-based business idea (length unconfirmed)
CVs of all team members (unconfirmed)
Named academic mentor at the host institution (secondary source)
Host institution's commitment to provide a workspace and founding-network support (secondary source)
Application forms per the EXIST guideline (unconfirmed)
decisionTime: unconfirmed
obligations: unconfirmed: reporting under the EXIST guideline; the host institution supervises the 12 months.
forkmeshAngle: Only if team members are recent graduates or researchers at a German university: a pre-founding stipend year to build a German entity around ForkMesh's hosted services and mirror fleet. EXIST funds tech-based founders coming out of academia.
risks: Needs a German academic affiliation and likely a not-yet-founded company. Pays personal stipends, not company funding. DATIpilot no longer takes submissions, and its 2026 'Transfer Scale-up' call is only for already-funded Innovationssprints.

amountText: Grant (subvention) of up to EUR 30,000 'sous condition', covering up to 50% of eligible expenses and, depending on company category, up to 70%; programme up to 24 months
eligibility: SMEs under the European definition with a high-technology-risk innovation project at maturation or feasibility stage. Expenses incurred before the application is filed are not eligible. Secondary sources add: registered in France for under one year, fewer than 50 employees, and at least 30% self-financing (unconfirmed on the official page).
entityTypes: French SMEs (for-profit start-ups)
process: 1. Contact Bpifrance through the offer page or a regional office. 2. File the aid request before incurring the project expenses. 3. Bpifrance reviews the request. 4. Sign the contract; the first tranche is paid at signature (after any conditions are lifted). 5. The balance is paid at completion after an end-of-programme report and a statement of paid expenses.
requiredMaterials: Aid request to Bpifrance describing the innovation project, its technical risks and maturation/feasibility work (form contents unconfirmed)
Budget of internal and external R&D expenses
Company registration and SME status documents (unconfirmed)
At completion: end-of-programme report and summary statement of expenses paid
decisionTime: unconfirmed
obligations: Two-tranche payment, final technical report and expense statement; the company co-finances the rest. No application or processing fees.
forkmeshAngle: If ForkMesh incorporates in France, use it for the maturation and feasibility phase of the hosted mirror fleet and the desktop node's isolated agent runner. Bpifrance funds early innovation projects with high technology risk.
risks: Needs a young French company. Small amount. The rule against costs incurred before filing means timing matters. The i-Nov competition (also listed in the brief) was not checked and runs in themed waves.

amountText: Up to EUR 10,000 per Pioniers project
eligibility: Natural or legal persons; individuals and students can apply. For 2026 the project must contribute to a 'Sterk internet' and be relevant to Dutch internet infrastructure while being broadly applicable. Impact should start in the Netherlands, and collaboration with Dutch internet-sector partners is a plus. Purely B2B projects, projects benefiting a single company or person, sponsorship/events and structural overhead are excluded.
entityTypes: Individuals, students, non-profits, companies (requests above EUR 10,000 need a legal entity)
process: 1. Optionally test the idea with the 'Toets je idee' web form or the Pioniers Quickscan. 2. Submit the Pioniersaanvraag in FundPro. 3. Staff and an advisory board from the Dutch internet community review it. 4. Answer within six weeks. 5. Run the project within six months and share the results.
requiredMaterials: Online questionnaire in FundPro
Short video pitch
Chamber of Commerce (KvK) extract (organisations)
Annual accounts (organisations)
decisionTime: Within six weeks of submission
obligations: Results and knowledge must be shared openly and be available to everyone; the project must finish within six months; general SIDN fonds terms apply.
forkmeshAngle: Pilot ForkMesh mirrors for Dutch open-source projects or public-sector Git repositories so their code stays reachable if a foreign host fails or blocks access. That fits the fund's strong-internet and digital-autonomy focus.
risks: Small grant. Needs clear relevance to the Netherlands and ideally Dutch partners. Projects that mainly benefit one company are excluded. Larger themed calls (e.g., the past 'transitie naar digitale autonomie' call) come 1-2 times a year, and none is open now.

funder: CSIRO (Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation, Australian Government)
amountText: AUD 20,000 - 60,000 dollar-matched funding for R&D with CSIRO researchers, projects up to 12 months
eligibility: Australian start-ups or SMEs with annual turnover and operating expenditure under AUD 10 million, or trading for less than three years. Must hold an ACN or ICN, be registered for GST, and be able to provide matching funding.
entityTypes: Australian companies (ACN) or incorporated bodies (ICN)
process: 1. Check eligibility. 2. Email the expression-of-interest form (DOCX) to the Kick-Start team. 3. CSIRO assesses the EOI, helps shape the project and matches a research team. 4. Scope, deliver and evaluate the project with the CSIRO team.
requiredMaterials: Kick-Start expression of interest form (DOCX)
ACN or ICN
GST registration
Evidence of the business's matching cash contribution
decisionTime: unconfirmed
obligations: Matched funding from the business; IP, reporting and contract terms not stated (ask the Kick-Start team).
forkmeshAngle: Commission CSIRO cyber-security researchers (team matched by CSIRO) to formally analyse or benchmark ForkMesh's signed-mirror protocol and integrity checks. Kick-Start exists to connect young Australian tech firms with CSIRO research capability.
risks: Needs an Australian entity. Small, matched funding that pays for CSIRO research rather than ForkMesh salaries. The Industry Growth Program is paused to new applications, AEA Ignite is for university researchers and closed in March 2026, and no open federal cyber-security business grant was found.

amountText: POC grant cap SGD 400,000; POV grant cap SGD 800,000 (raised on 2 Jan 2025); paid on milestones; Enterprise Singapore holds a right to subscribe for shares (equity component)
eligibility: Singapore private limited start-ups registered within the past 10 years, with at least 30% local equity held by Singaporeans/PRs, not a corporate subsidiary at incorporation, group turnover at most SGD 100 million or at most 200 workers, and core R&D in Singapore. Must have proprietary technology (integrating off-the-shelf components does not count). Paid-up capital must be at least 10% (POC) or 20% (POV) of the grant.
entityTypes: Singapore-incorporated private limited companies (public-sector research PIs for POC)
process: 1. Download and fill in the Startup SG Tech Registration of Interest form. 2. Submit it via go.gov.sg/askenterprisesg. 3. Discuss scope with an Enterprise Singapore officer. 4. Submit the formal Stage 2 application (POC or POV). 5. Milestone-based grant with an equity subscription right.
requiredMaterials: Startup SG Tech Registration of Interest form
Formal Stage 2 application (contents unconfirmed)
Evidence of paid-up capital (at least 10% of a POC grant or 20% of a POV grant)
Explanation of the science/technology and proprietary IP or intellectual assets owned by the startup
For POV: proof of interest from a potential customer or third-party investor and evidence of business competencies
decisionTime: unconfirmed
obligations: Milestone-based payments; Enterprise Singapore's share-subscription right; one project at a time; core R&D in Singapore.
forkmeshAngle: With a Singapore entity, a POC grant could fund the proprietary layer around the open protocol, such as hosted mirror-fleet orchestration and the runner tier. The scheme funds commercialisation of proprietary, scalable technology.
risks: Needs 30% local shareholding and R&D in Singapore. The equity component dilutes ownership. An MIT-licensed core may not count as proprietary IP. IMDA alternatives were not checked.

amountText: Maximum SEK 500,000, up to 100% of project costs, max 9 months
eligibility: Swedish limited companies (aktiebolag) operating in Sweden: unlisted, no profit distributed last year, net turnover or balance sheet total of SEK 10 million or less (only one may be exceeded), max 10 FTE employees, at most 10 years old on 23 March 2027. No funding from Innovative Startups 2025. One proposal per company.
entityTypes: Swedish limited companies (aktiebolag) only
process: 1. Attend an info meeting (2 or 9 November 2026). 2. Apply in Vinnova's portal in Swedish or English by 12 January 2027, 14:00. 3. Three experts score potential, implementability and team. 4. Proposals are rejected or placed in a randomised group when the budget is short. 5. Decision on 23 March 2027; project starts by 1 April 2027.
requiredMaterials: Vinnova application form covering the project, participants and budget
Budget by cost type (personnel, equipment, consultancy and licensing with justification, other direct costs, indirect costs at most 30% of wage costs)
Company eligibility information (size, turnover, age, ownership)
unconfirmed: de minimis declaration for companies aged 5-10 years
decisionTime: Decision on 23 March 2027 (about 10 weeks after close)
obligations: Sign the grant agreement; report progress, costs and results; follow the rules on use of results; repay if paid too much or if terms are breached; GBER Article 22 or de minimis state-aid rules apply.
forkmeshAngle: If ForkMesh is a young Swedish AB, test customer needs and willingness to pay for the bounded hosted services (managed mirrors, runner tier) with European development teams. Vinnova funds early market validation of innovations that can compete globally.
risks: Needs a small, young Swedish AB. Selection is partly by lottery. Small amount.

program: Ecosystem Support Program (ESP) - Wishlist and RFP grants
amountText: No fixed range: funding depends on scope and complexity unless the Wishlist/RFP item states a budget; ESP expects rates somewhat below market. Paid on-chain in ETH by default.
deadline: unconfirmed: no active Wishlist or RFP items listed on 2026-10-16; new items are posted periodically (next ones not dated)
eligibility: Teams and individuals building free, open-source, non-commercial work aligned with CROPS (censorship resistance, open source, privacy, security) that enables Ethereum builders. For-profit companies may apply if the grant-funded work is open source and accessible to the community. Must apply against a specific posted Wishlist or RFP item (general open applications were discontinued in late 2025).
geography: Worldwide (subject to identity verification and sanctions screening at onboarding)
entityTypes: For-profit, nonprofit, individuals, academic teams
process: 1. Browse the posted Wishlist items (problem areas) or RFPs (scoped, time-bound deliverables). 2. Submit one application per item via the item's form with methodology, timeline and deliverables; a confirmation email follows. 3. Review by the grants-management team with the relevant EF team, possibly an interview, rescoping or budget negotiation. 4. Decision by email. 5. Onboarding (identity verification, formal grant letter), then execution with a Grant Evaluator doing check-ins and milestone reviews. 6. Publish results in a public report or post.
requiredMaterials: Selection of the specific Wishlist or RFP item being addressed (separate application per item)
Team / applicant background and relevant experience
Proposed approach and methodology
Timeline with milestones
Concrete deliverables
Budget request (negotiable with the GM team; RFPs may give budget guidance)
Identity verification documents and signed grant letter at onboarding
ETH-capable wallet address for on-chain payment
decisionTime: Most applications reviewed within 3-6 weeks of submission
obligations: Milestone-based payments (ETH on-chain by default); check-ins with a Grant Evaluator; outputs must remain open source; public report or post on completion. No equity.
forkmeshAngle: Propose ForkMesh's signed, integrity-checked Git mirror network as censorship-resistant source hosting for Ethereum client and tooling repositories, so that client code stays clonable if a central forge removes or loses it. This matches ESP's CROPS mandate (censorship resistance, open source, security) and the EF's concern for client diversity and supply-chain integrity; the pitch should target a matching Wishlist/RFP item when one is posted.
risks: No open Wishlist or RFP items on 2026-10-16, so ForkMesh must wait for a fitting item and cannot pitch unsolicited. Funded work must be non-commercial, which conflicts with ForkMesh's paid hosted tier unless the proposal is scoped to the MIT protocol/mirror code. Ethereum-specific relevance must be argued since ForkMesh references Solana for payouts. Payment in ETH carries price risk.

amountText: Open Grants applications for funding up to $50,000
eligibility: Individuals or organisations proposing novel work that advances the Filecoin network (developer and data tooling, integrations, research and protocols, storage, retrieval, FVM). The program prioritises Filecoin-network functionality and de-emphasises IPFS/libp2p-only projects. The agreement and payments must be with the same individual or entity that applies.
geography: Worldwide (unconfirmed: sanctions/KYC restrictions apply at contracting)
entityTypes: Individuals, for-profit, nonprofit
process: 1. Open a GitHub issue in filecoin-project/devgrants using the Open Grant Application template. 2. Continuous review; the committee comments with questions or change requests on the issue. 3. Preliminary review update within about 2 weeks. 4. Final decision generally within 4 weeks of submission. 5. Sign the Open Source Software Grant Agreement with the work plan and funding milestones (no work before signature). 6. Deliver milestones and get paid per milestone.
requiredMaterials: Project name and proposal category (Developer and data tooling, Integrations, Research & protocols, Storage, Retrieval, FVM, Other)
Individual or entity name (must match contracting/payment party)
Proposer GitHub username and project repo(s)
Optional: Filecoin/Protocol Labs network affiliations and technical sponsor
Yes/No agreement to open-source all work under MIT/Apache-2 dual licence
Project Summary (2-3 paragraphs)
Impact (2-3 paragraphs: pain points, benefits, risks, success)
Outcomes and deliverables with success metrics
Data onboarding projections at months 1, 3, 6, 12 (if onboarding data to Filecoin)
Adoption, reach and growth strategy (first 10 / 100 users)
Development roadmap of 2-4 milestones (aim for 1-2 pages): functionality, people and roles, funding and real dates per milestone
Total budget table (milestone, description, deliverables, completion date, funding)
Maintenance and upgrade plans
Team members, LinkedIn profiles, team website (https), relevant experience, prior code repositories
How you heard of the program and contact email
decisionTime: Preliminary update within ~2 weeks; final decision generally within 4 weeks of submission
obligations: Signed Open Source Software Grant Agreement; milestone-based funding; all funded work open-sourced under MIT/Apache-2 dual licence; no work before both parties sign. No equity.
forkmeshAngle: Propose a Filecoin archival backend for ForkMesh: mirror nodes periodically seal signed repository snapshots (Git packs plus signed issue/PR records) into Filecoin deals and can restore a repo from Filecoin when every live mirror is gone, under the Developer and data tooling or Integrations category. This adds steady real data onboarding (source-code preservation) and a Web2 developer-tool integration, both of which the program asks for.
risks: Proposal is public as a GitHub issue. ForkMesh's code is MIT; the grant asks for MIT/Apache-2 dual licence on funded work (compatible but needs a decision). Must show Filecoin-network usage (data onboarding), not just IPFS. Heavy volume of AI-generated proposals in the queue (several per day in Oct 2026) raises competition. Payment currency (FIL or fiat) unconfirmed.

program: Solana Foundation Grants (standard and convertible milestone grants, RFPs)
amountText: No per-grant amount stated; the Foundation cites $100M+ committed across 500+ projects. Milestone-based. (Superteam microgrants, a separate track, are up to $10k.)
eligibility: Anyone (individuals, teams, companies, nonprofits, universities, governments) building a public good for the Solana ecosystem: a significant open-source contribution, a meaningful free community offering, or a novel proof of concept, and able to explain why it is only possible on Solana. Projects with a commercial component are steered to convertible grants.
geography: Worldwide (unconfirmed: sanctioned jurisdictions presumably excluded at contracting)
entityTypes: Individuals, for-profit, nonprofit, universities, governments
process: 1. Optionally browse the Foundation RFP list (Airtable) for a matching request. 2. Submit the Foundation Grants form (HubSpot) with overview, public-good case, budget and milestones. 3. Rolling review (about 1 week); subject-matter experts may schedule a call for technical due diligence and market research. 4. Decision by email (about 3 weeks). 5. Negotiate and sign the grant agreement with the Foundation legal team (standard or convertible). 6. Deliver milestones; funds released per milestone.
requiredMaterials: Project overview
Explanation of how the project is a public good for Solana and why it is only possible on Solana
Structured budget
Clear, measurable funding milestones tied to community impact
Open-source repository / plan to open-source learnings
Contact email for decision
unconfirmed: exact HubSpot form fields (not shown on the official page)
decisionTime: About 1 week review plus about 3 weeks to decision (official page); rolling
obligations: Milestone-based payments under a signed grant agreement; open-source / public-good deliverables. Convertible grants convert into an investment once agreed milestones are met (equity/token-like obligation for commercial projects).
forkmeshAngle: Propose open-sourcing ForkMesh's Solana-based community payout pool as a reusable public good: self-custodial contributor wallets, on-chain payouts for merged pull requests and mirror hosting, all keyed to signed Git records, usable by any open-source project. ForkMesh already references Solana for payouts, so the 'only possible on Solana' case (cheap, fast micro-payouts to many contributors) is natural and the Foundation funds developer public goods.
risks: Funding is only for the Solana-specific public-good part; the hosted paid tier would push the Foundation toward a convertible grant (investment-like obligation). No stated grant size; third-party guides (unverified) suggest typical grants of USD 10k-50k. Crypto payouts may raise regulatory/KYC questions depending on ForkMesh's jurisdiction.

amountText: No amount stated; grant sizes vary by project scope and impact and are paid in bitcoin
eligibility: Software developers, activists, educators, community builders, translators and UX designers working on Bitcoin and complementary freedom technology (Bitcoin Core, Nostr, Ecash, Bitcoin utility apps) that serves human-rights defenders in repressive settings. Non-Bitcoin cryptocurrencies and projects outside HRF's mission are not funded. Unsuccessful applicants may reapply in later rounds.

Expect further information within 4-6 weeks. 4. Grantees are announced in an end-of-quarter press release. 5. HRF finalises administrative details and delivers the grant in bitcoin; the team supports the project during the work.
requiredMaterials: Brief project description
unconfirmed: individual form fields (not listed on the official page)
Bitcoin receiving address for payment (grants are delivered in bitcoin)

Documentation of development practices and processes
Previous security reviews, including of dependencies
Security policy (e.g. SECURITY.md)
List of any components that are not open source

Cryptographic libraries used

A published audit makes ForkMesh's supply-chain-integrity claims credible, and OSTIF's sponsors fund exactly this kind of supply-chain security work.
risks: Not a guaranteed grant: the audit happens only if OSTIF or the project finds sponsors to pay USD 30k-200k. Sponsors favour widely used critical projects, and ForkMesh is early-stage. Findings become public after the disclosure window.

Existing 1Password Teams account with at least two owners
